pages.name: An arrow called a
pages.text: A [[vector]] is a size with a direction, drawn as an arrow. Arrow `a` runs 3 squares across and 4 up. The two moves meet at a right angle, so Pythagoras gives its length: `√(3² + 4²) = 5`. That length is its size. We write it `|a| = 5`, and books call it the [[magnitude]]. Its moves and size change whenever its tip moves.

pages.name: Mass or weight
pages.task: A [[scalar]] has a size but no direction. This pump has a mass, a temperature and a weight. Which of the three is a vector?
pages.why: Weight is a force pulling the pump down. It has a size and a direction, so it is a vector. The 500 kg mass and the 40 °C temperature are sizes alone, so they are scalars.

pages.text: Arrow `a` has slid to a new place on the grid, and a faint copy stays where it began. It still runs 3 across and 4 up, with size 5. Where an arrow sits is not part of it, so it is still `a`.

pages.name: Which one is a?
pages.task: Which arrow is the same vector as `a`?
pages.why: `b` runs 3 across and 4 up, just like `a`. The same size and the same direction make the same vector, wherever it sits. `c` and `d` have size 5 too, but they point other ways.

pages.name: From A to B
pages.text: The arrow from point A to point B is the vector `AB`. It runs 3 across and 4 up, the same moves as `a`, so `AB = a`. Going from B back to A covers the same ground the other way. In print a vector's name is bold. By hand you underline it.

pages.name: Back from B to A
pages.task: Left and down count as minus. What are the moves of `BA`, from B back to A?
pages.why: From B, 3 left and 4 down lands on A. Those are the moves of `AB` with both signs changed. Moving backwards along a vector makes it negative, so `BA = −AB`.

pages.name: A number in front
pages.text: A number in front scales a vector. `2a` is `a` done twice: 6 across and 8 up, size 10. At 0 the arrow shrinks to a dot, and below 0 it points the other way. `a`, `2a` and `−a` lie along one line, so they are parallel.

pages.name: Minus two
pages.why: `−2a` multiplies both moves by −2, giving 6 left and 8 down. The minus turns it round. Its size is still 10, never −10, because a length cannot be below zero.

pages.name: Size 1
pages.text: Divide both moves by the size, 5, and `a` shrinks to length 1 along the same line. That is its [[unit vector]]: 0.6 across and 0.8 up. It holds the direction alone.

pages.name: Unit vector of 2a
pages.task: `2a` runs 6 across and 8 up, with size 10. What is its unit vector?
pages.why: Divide both moves by the size, 10, to get 0.6 across and 0.8 up. Its size is `√(0.6² + 0.8²) = 1`. It matches the unit vector of `a`, because `2a` points the same way.

pages.name: Round in a circle
pages.task: A boat goes round a circle at a steady 12 knots. What stays the same all the way round?
pages.why: Speed is a size alone, and it stays 12 knots. Velocity is the speed with its direction. The direction turns all the way round, so the velocity keeps changing.

pages.name: Turn it round
pages.task: A boat's velocity `v` is 3 m/s east and 4 m/s north. It reverses course at the same speed. What is `−v`?
pages.why: `−v` changes the sign of both moves: 3 m/s west and 4 m/s south. Its speed is still `√(3² + 4²) = 5` m/s. Only the direction has turned round.
